# Set Up Reduce Interruptions Focus with Apple Intelligence Filtering

> **In short:** Turn on the built-in Reduce Interruptions Focus in iOS, and Apple Intelligence (Apple's on-device AI) will quietly filter which notifications break through — so only the messages that truly matter can buzz your iPhone. You need a supported iPhone and Apple Intelligence enabled first.

Notification overload has become the new normal — your phone buzzes through the day with group chats, delivery updates, game pings, and news alerts, and most of them don't actually need you right now. The Reduce Interruptions Focus, paired with Apple Intelligence, is Apple's answer: your iPhone decides which notifications deserve your attention and silences the rest. This guide walks you through setting it up in about five minutes, even if you've never opened the Focus menu before.

## Before you start
- **An iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence.** Apple currently lists iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, and the iPhone 16 family (and newer supported models). If you have an older iPhone, you can still use the basic Focus, but the smart AI filter won't appear.
- **iOS 18.1 or later.** To check, open **Settings → General → Software Update**.
- **About 5 minutes**, and a strong Wi-Fi connection — the first-time Apple Intelligence setup downloads a small model in the background.

## Step 1 — Make sure Apple Intelligence is ready

Open the **Settings** app and scroll down to **Apple Intelligence & Siri** (sometimes labeled simply "Apple Intelligence"). Tap it. On the screen that opens, look for an **Apple Intelligence** toggle near the top. If it is off, tap it to switch it on. The first time you turn it on, your iPhone will quietly download a small AI model in the background — this can take a few minutes on Wi-Fi, so keep your phone on a strong network while you wait.

💬 Example: None — this is just a toggle switch.

**If it looks different:** If you don't see "Apple Intelligence & Siri" anywhere in Settings, your iPhone model likely doesn't support it. The basic Focus modes still work without it, but Step 5 below won't apply to you.

You'll know it worked when the toggle turns green and you see a message along the lines of "Apple Intelligence is ready" — or when the download finishes without showing an error.

## Step 2 — Open the Focus settings

Still inside **Settings**, scroll until you find **Focus** and tap it. You'll see a list of built-in Focus modes — things like **Do Not Disturb**, **Sleep**, **Work**, **Personal**, and **Reading**. A small moon icon usually marks whichever Focus is currently active, and there's a **+** (plus) button at the top right of the screen for adding new ones.

💬 Example: None — this is just navigation.

**If it looks different:** If "Focus" doesn't appear in the list, swipe down from the middle of the Settings screen to open a search bar at the top, type "Focus", and tap the result.

You'll know it worked when you can see the list of Focus modes and there's a clear way to add or pick one.

## Step 3 — Pick the Reduce Interruptions Focus

Tap **Reduce Interruptions** in the list. If it isn't there, tap the **+** button and choose it from the suggested options — it's one of Apple's built-in Focus modes. Once it's selected, you'll land on a setup screen with sections like **People** and **Apps**, plus an option related to Apple Intelligence. This Focus is special: it's designed to be the quietest mode, with optional smart filtering layered on top.

💬 Example: None — this is just a selection.

**If it looks different:** On older iOS versions, you might see only "Do Not Disturb" instead. The Apple Intelligence smart filter (Step 5) is tied specifically to the Reduce Interruptions Focus, so if you don't see it, update to a newer iOS first.

You'll know it worked when you're on the Reduce Interruptions screen and can see sections for choosing who and what can still reach you.

## Step 4 — Choose the people and apps that can still notify you

Tap **People** to pick contacts, then tap **Apps** to pick apps that are allowed to break through the Focus. Use the **+** buttons to add entries from your contacts and from your installed apps. Only the people and apps you select here will be able to buzz your phone or pop a banner — everything else is silenced.

💬 Example: Add your partner and your manager to People. Add Phone, Messages, and your work chat to Apps. Keep it short — three to five entries is plenty to start.

**If it looks different:** If you can't find the "People" or "Apps" sections, scroll down inside the Focus settings — they may be tucked under a "Customize Screens" or "Filter" group, depending on your iOS version.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows at least one or two contacts and apps you've selected, and you can come back to edit this list any time.

## Step 5 — Turn on Apple Intelligence's smart filtering

Scroll down inside the Reduce Interruptions Focus and look for an option that mentions **filtering notifications with Apple Intelligence** (the exact label can vary slightly by iOS version, but it usually includes the words "Apple Intelligence" and "Filter"). Toggle it on. When you do, a short description explains that Apple Intelligence will decide which notifications are important enough to break through your Focus.

💬 Example: None — this is just a toggle.

**If it looks different:** If this option is missing, double-check that Apple Intelligence is on (Step 1), that your iPhone and language are supported, and that your iOS is up to date. Apple Intelligence features also roll out gradually by region and language, so it may not be in your area yet.

You'll know it worked when the toggle is green and the first time a notification comes in, you may notice a small Apple Intelligence-style badge on it, indicating the filter decided to let it through.

## Step 6 — Turn the Focus on and test it

Swipe down from the **top-right corner** of your iPhone screen to open **Control Center** (a small square panel of quick toggles). Tap the **Focus** button — it usually looks like a crescent moon — and pick **Reduce Interruptions** from the list that appears. A small moon icon will appear in your status bar at the top of the screen, confirming the Focus is active. Now use your phone normally for an hour or two. Most notifications will be quietly sent to Notification Center (the swipe-down list) without buzzing you, and only the ones that matter — a call from your partner, a message flagged as time-sensitive — will actually interrupt you.

💬 Example: None — just turn it on and use your phone normally.

**If it looks different:** If you can't find the Focus button in Control Center, go back to **Settings → Focus → Reduce Interruptions** and use the **Turn On** option directly on that screen. On some iOS versions, the Focus controls also live under the **Lock Screen** long-press menu.

You'll know it worked when you see the small moon icon in the top status bar, and when an unimportant notification (a game promo, a sale alert) arrives silently in Notification Center instead of buzzing the screen.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the Apple Intelligence toggle in Step 1.** If the smart filter option never shows up in Step 5, it's almost always because Apple Intelligence wasn't turned on first — or your iPhone doesn't support it. Go back to Step 1 before troubleshooting anything else.
- **Adding too many people or apps to the allow list.** The whole point of this Focus is calm. Start with two or three entries and add more only if you genuinely miss something. If you let everything through, the AI filter has nothing left to do.
- **Giving up after one missed notification.** Apple Intelligence learns from your habits over a few days. The first day might feel "wrong" — a message you wanted slipped through silently. Give it a week before deciding it isn't for you.
- **Worrying that the AI is sending your notifications to a server to be read.** Apple Intelligence processes much of this on-device, and the cloud portion uses Apple's Private Cloud Compute, which is designed so your content isn't stored or read by humans. Your messages stay yours.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** A dinner with family or a walk in the park stops being interrupted by 30 random buzzes. The people who really need you still get through; the noise doesn't.
- **For your business or work:** A two-hour deep work block stays deep. The smart filter learns that a casual team chat ping is less urgent than a client email marked important — and acts accordingly.
- **If you're just getting started:** Turn the Focus on for one meeting this week. Notice what got through, and what didn't. That's all you need to start feeling the difference.

## Try it now
Open **Settings → Focus** and just look at the list of Focus modes — don't change anything yet. Seeing the names in one place is the first step toward actually using one, and the menu is friendlier than it looks.
